judge.voice: Fine, B2, not the C1 I told you, but it did not feel arbitrary. The tasks were what I do every day: supplier deadlines, the director, push-back. Nothing babyish, nothing slow, and I finished in about seven minutes instead of a written test plus an oral part. It showed my own sentences, and 'more better' was fair, I admit. What I miss is more bite. I wrote 'since 2015' with a present tense and 'I don't want that we deliver', and nobody mentioned them. I suspect my director would notice those. The summary is also a bit soft: 'grammar slips' tells me nothing I can fix. I'd use it again before a call if it called out my repeated mistakes by name. I'd tell a colleague it's quick and credible, but not yet sharp.
